schreiben.check.a1-formular-anmeldung.0: “Nombre” is your first name; “apellidos” are your surnames. Many Spanish forms ask for two (“primer” and “segundo apellido”). If you only have one, leave the second empty.
schreiben.check.a1-formular-anmeldung.1: The date is day/month/year: 04/03/1996. 03/04/1996 would be 3 April.
schreiben.check.a1-formular-anmeldung.2: “Código postal” and “municipio” go in separate fields, even if they are together in the text.
schreiben.check.a1-nachricht-absage.0: All four points are there: in an exam, a missing point costs more than a small grammar mistake.
schreiben.check.a1-nachricht-absage.1: There is a greeting and a sign-off (¡Hola, Lucía! / Un abrazo).
schreiben.check.a1-nachricht-absage.2: Questions and exclamations open and close: ¿…? and ¡…!
schreiben.check.a1-nachricht-absage.3: The sentences are short. At A1, “Tengo que trabajar.” is better than a long sentence with a mistake.
schreiben.check.a2-email-nachbarn.0: The requests are questions (“¿Podría…?”, “¿Le importaría…?”), not orders (“Riegue mis plantas”, “Tiene que…”).
schreiben.check.a2-email-nachbarn.1: After “¿Le importaría…?” comes the infinitive: “¿Le importaría recoger mis cartas?”.
schreiben.check.a2-email-nachbarn.2: “Usted” all the way through: “le llevo”, “su ayuda”, “podría”. One “tú” in the middle would stand out.
schreiben.check.a2-email-nachbarn.3: Greeting and sign-off match: “Buenos días, señora Ortega:” → “Un saludo”. “Un beso” is too familiar for a neighbour you hardly know.
schreiben.check.a2-email-school.0: “Está enfermo” with “estar”, because being ill is a state: “es enfermo” is a typical mistake.
schreiben.check.a2-email-school.1: The teacher can tell at once which child and which class it is about.
schreiben.check.a2-email-school.2: A polite question: “¿Podría decirme…?”. Some schools use “tú” with parents; “usted” is the safe choice in a first message.
schreiben.check.a2-formular-arztpraxis.0: Numbers are spoken, not written: “el veinte de noviembre de mil novecientos ochenta y ocho” → 20/11/1988. Spaniards often say a mobile number in groups: “seiscientos, cero cero cero, trescientos quince”.
schreiben.check.a2-formular-arztpraxis.1: Careful with “¿Primera cita?”. He answers “No” to a different question (“¿Ha venido antes?”), so here the right answer is “sí”.
schreiben.check.a2-formular-arztpraxis.2: “Perfecto” means the appointment is confirmed, so fill in the doctor, the date and the time. “Las tres y media de la tarde” is 15:30.
schreiben.check.a2-padron-form.0: A Spanish address runs street, number, floor, door: “calle de las Eras, 5, 1.º B”.
schreiben.check.a2-padron-form.1: “Municipio anterior” asks where you lived before: Murcia, not Valdelora and not Tánger.
schreiben.check.a2-padron-form.2: Copy your document number exactly, letter by letter. The number here is a made-up example.
schreiben.check.a2-padron-form.3: This is language practice, not official guidance: the real form and the papers to bring vary, so ask at your own “ayuntamiento”.
schreiben.check.b1-email-landlord.0: All four points are there, and the landlady can act on them: what is broken, since when, when someone can come.
schreiben.check.b1-email-landlord.1: The tenses tell the story: “se estropeó el lunes” (one event) and “no tenemos” after “desde entonces” (still true now).
schreiben.check.b1-email-landlord.2: “Usted” throughout, and a colon after the greeting: “Estimada señora Ibáñez:”. In a formal letter, Spanish uses a colon there, not a comma.
schreiben.check.b1-email-landlord.3: “Prefiere que lo llame yo”: “preferir que” takes the subjunctive.
schreiben.check.b1-email-employer.0: A solution comes with the request: the boss reads “puedo cambiar el turno con Jordi” and only has to say yes.
schreiben.check.b1-email-employer.1: “Tú” with your boss is normal in many Spanish workplaces. If yours uses “usted”, keep to it: “Le escribo para pedirle…”.
schreiben.check.b1-email-employer.2: The tone is a request, not an announcement: “Si te parece bien” softens it.
schreiben.check.b1-email-employer.3: Time off for official appointments depends on your contract and your “convenio”; this task practises the email, not your rights.
schreiben.check.b2-beschwerde-reiseveran: No angry words: “Lamento comunicarles que surgieron varios problemas graves” instead of “es una vergüenza”. At B2 the tone is part of the mark: firm, but never rude.
Each problem is set against a promise (“En su folleto se describía… Sin embargo, en realidad…”). A complaint without that comparison is only an opinion.
There is a clear demand AND a deadline. Without a date, a letter of complaint is not complete.
B2 linking words and forms: “dado que”, “además”, “sin embargo”, “por ello”, “sin que” + subjunctive. “Estimados señores:” with a colon, then “Atentamente”.
schreiben.check.b2-opinion-text.0: The position is clear in the first paragraph, and the last paragraph comes back to it.
schreiben.check.b2-opinion-text.1: Each argument has an example of its own. “Sería más seguro” alone is a claim; the two streets on the way to school make it real.
schreiben.check.b2-opinion-text.2: The other side gets a fair sentence before the answer: “Es cierto que…; sin embargo…”.
schreiben.check.b2-opinion-text.3: B2 forms: the conditional for what would happen (“mejoraría”, “ganaría”), “no se trata de…, sino de…”, “prefiero que” + subjunctive.
schreiben.check.b1-formular-vhs.0: Every field is filled in. An empty field counts as a mistake, even if the information is in the text.
schreiben.check.b1-formular-vhs.1: Copy names, numbers and dates exactly as they are in the text, with their accents; in Spain the day comes before the month (12 de septiembre, 12/09).
schreiben.check.b1-formular-vhs.2: Nothing made up: if something is not in the text, leave the field empty or put a dash.
schreiben.check.b1-brief-david.0: Every point in the task is covered. A missing point costs more than three grammar mistakes.
schreiben.check.b1-brief-david.1: Greeting and sign-off suit each other and the person (¡Hola, Javier! … Un abrazo).
schreiben.check.b1-brief-david.2: The sentences are linked (así que, porque, pero, además, aunque), not just one after the other.
schreiben.check.b1-fehlerjagd.0: Read first, then compare: discuss the text only once you have marked every mistake you can find.
schreiben.check.b1-fehlerjagd.1: The text has about 20 mistakes. Look at: ser or estar, gender, “desde” or “desde hace”, irregular participles, the subjunctive after “me gustaría que”, accents, “¿…?”, capital letters in dates, the punctuation after the greeting, and two closing lines translated word for word from English.
schreiben.check.b1-fehlerjagd.2: Write down the mistakes you make yourself, too. That is the point of the task.
ac.find.rr: “{word}” has r: a single r is one quick tap of the tongue tip, rr and a first r are several. pero is not perro.
ac.find.cz: “{word}”: z, and c before e or i, are like th in “think” in Spain: tongue tip between your teeth. Not ts, not ch, no buzz.
ac.find.jg: “{word}”: j, and g before e or i, are a rasp at the back of your mouth, like ch in Scottish “loch”.
ac.find.bv: “{word}”: b and v are one sound. Use only your lips; your top teeth don't touch your lip.
ac.find.vokale: “{word}”: keep every vowel short and clear, stressed or not. No glide, no weak “uh”.
ac.find.aspiration: “{word}” has p, t or k. Say it with no puff of air.
ac.find.dsuave: The d in “{word}” is soft, like th in “this”. The tongue only just touches your teeth.
ac.find.lly: “{word}”: ll and y sound like y in “yes” in most of Spain. Never an l.
ac.find.nasal: “{word}”: keep the vowel clean, with no air through your nose, then say a real n or m.
ac.find.u: “{word}” has u: round your lips and pull your tongue back, like the “ou” of French “vous”.
ac.find.ch: “{word}” has ch, as in “church”. Not sh, not k.
ac.find.enlace: “{word}” follows straight on from the word before. No small stop in your throat.
ac.find.doble: “{word}”: the consonants are short. Don't hold them; move straight on to the next vowel.
ac.find.g: “{word}” has g as in “go”, made at the back of your mouth. Not h.

delesiele.title: DELE or SIELE?
delesiele.lead: Both are serious Spanish exams, and the Instituto Cervantes is behind both. What decides between them is what you need the result for. For Spanish nationality, the answer is the DELE. For almost everything else, ask the institution first.
delesiele.purpose.title: What do you need it for?
delesiele.purpose.note: General orientation, not legal advice. Rules change, so before you pay for an exam, check with the office that will read your result.
delesiele.compare.title: The two exams side by side
delesiele.compare.note: Checked in November 2026. Prices are what some exam centres in Spain listed and aren't an official tariff: they change every year and differ by country and centre. DELE timings and rules vary by source, so check them in the current exam guide.
delesiele.tips.title: If you still can't decide
delesiele.tips.1: You don't know your level: the SIELE places you wherever you are, while a DELE at the wrong level can end in No apto.
delesiele.tips.2: You freeze when you talk to a computer: the DELE has examiners in the room. You get nervous in front of people: the SIELE is recorded.
delesiele.tips.3: You need a result soon: the SIELE's flexible dates and quicker results usually help. Check that the institution accepts it first.
delesiele.tips.4: You want something that doesn't run out: the DELE has no expiry date as far as we could check, while a SIELE result lasts five years.
delesiele.tips.5: You only learn Spain's Spanish: the SIELE site says the exam uses varieties from across the Spanish-speaking world, so practise hearing other accents too.

testdaf.bands.title: How scores match levels
testdaf.bands.text: Each test has its own table, so the same score can mean different levels: 120 points is B1 in reading but A2 in speaking. These are the points the exam guide lists for each level.
testdaf.bands.note: There is no pass mark: you always get a score. A score under the A1 line reaches no level, which the guide calls No apto. Reading and listening are marked automatically, with no points lost for wrong answers as far as the guide's formula shows, so answer everything. Writing and speaking go to trained raters.
testdaf.mod.title: SIELE Global or S1 to S5?
testdaf.mod.text: You can take all four tests or a combination. Only SIELE Global gives a certificate; the others give a report. Both are valid for five years. Before you choose one of the shorter options, ask whether your institution accepts a report.

testdaf.day.3: Speaking is recorded on the computer. Nobody answers you, so keep talking until the time is up.
testdaf.day.4: The exam uses Spanish from across the Spanish-speaking world, according to the SIELE site. Expect accents other than Spain's.
testdaf.day.5: Results come within three weeks at most, according to the SIELE site. An institution can check your result with the code on the document.

delesiele.p.nationality.title: Spanish nationality
delesiele.p.nationality.text: If you need a language exam for Spanish nationality, take the DELE at A2 or above. It goes together with the CCSE knowledge test. The SIELE's own site says that its certificates don't count for the nationality procedure. Some applicants are exempt from the language exam, for example people from countries where Spanish is an official language, so check your own case with the Ministry of Justice.
delesiele.p.university.title: University in Spain
delesiele.p.university.text: The SIELE site says that the Spanish rectors' conference (CRUE) and the university language centres' association (ACLES) list the SIELE as an accepted certificate. The site also says that many universities ask for B1 or B2. Even so, each university and each degree sets its own rule, so get it in writing from the admissions office. Ask how old your result may be, too.
delesiele.p.work.title: Work
delesiele.p.work.text: Private employers often care more about your level than about which exam it came from. The SIELE is quick to book if you need a result soon, and the DELE has no expiry date as far as we could check. Public jobs and regulated professions can have fixed rules. For the specialist training places in health (Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy and others), the SIELE site says the SIELE is recognised. Check the current call for applications.
delesiele.p.visa.title: Visas, scholarships and other official uses
delesiele.p.visa.answer: Read the rules of the procedure
delesiele.p.visa.text: We can't give a general answer here. A consulate, ministry or scholarship body says which certificates it accepts, at which level, and how old they may be. If the rules name only one exam, take that one. This page is general orientation, not legal advice.
delesiele.p.self.title: For yourself
delesiele.p.self.text: If you want a goal to work towards, the DELE gives you one level to aim for and a diploma if you reach it. If you want to see where you stand, the SIELE gives you a level for each skill, and you don't have to know your level before you book.

nat.title: Spanish nationality by residence: CCSE and DELE A2
nat.lead: To become Spanish through residence, most adults need years of legal residence, the CCSE test and a DELE A2 or higher. Here is who needs what, who is exempt and in what order to do things.
nat.legal: General orientation, not legal advice. We read the laws listed at the end of this page in Spain's official gazette (the BOE) on 6 November 2026. We haven't checked how each office applies them, and rules, forms and fees change. For your own case, check the Ministry of Justice's site, or ask an immigration lawyer or an advice organisation.
nat.short.title: The short version
nat.short.1: You have lived in Spain legally and without a break for the time that applies to you, right up to when you apply.
nat.short.2: You show that you are integrated: usually with the CCSE, plus a DELE A2 or higher unless you are exempt.
nat.short.3: You apply to the Ministry of Justice and pay a fee.
nat.short.4: If you get a yes, you have 180 days to take the oath at the Civil Registry and ask to be registered as Spanish.
nat.res.title: How long you must have lived in Spain
nat.res.2.who: Nationals by origin of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea or Portugal, and people of Sephardic origin.
nat.res.note: The Civil Code asks for residence that is legal, continuous and immediately before you apply. Time without a residence permit isn't legal residence. The article doesn't say how long you can be away, so ask before a long trip. You must also show good civic conduct and enough integration into Spanish society. (Código Civil, arts. 21 and 22.)
nat.tests.title: Who needs which test
nat.t.list.who: National of a country on the list below
nat.t.has.who: You already hold a DELE A2 or higher
nat.t.cert.who: You hold an official A2 or higher certificate from a Spanish education authority (ask how to submit it)
nat.t.minor.who: Under 18, or your legal capacity was modified by a court
nat.t.eso.who: You went to school in Spain and passed ESO (compulsory secondary education)
nat.t.disp.who: You can't read or write, or you have learning difficulties
nat.list.title: Countries and territories exempt from the DELE
nat.list.text: The regulation names Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, Equatorial Guinea, Guatemala, Honduras, Mexico, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Puerto Rico, the Dominican Republic, Uruguay and Venezuela.
nat.list.warn: A short residence period doesn't mean no DELE. The 2-year period also covers people from Brazil, Portugal, Andorra and the Philippines, but these countries are not on the list, so their nationals need the DELE unless another exemption applies.
nat.disp.title: Asking for a dispensa
nat.disp.1: A dispensa is an official decision that excuses you from the tests. Ask for it on the Ministry of Justice's site before you apply for nationality. You can't start the nationality application until the dispensa is decided, and if you send both together, the nationality application is archived.
nat.disp.2: The decision can take up to six months, and no answer by then counts as a refusal. The Ministry can excuse you, refuse, or allow adapted tests at the Instituto Cervantes.
nat.disp.3: If you went to school in Spain and passed ESO, you don't need a separate request: you can apply for nationality directly, and your studies are checked.
nat.disp.4: For children of school age, a certificate from the school is required instead of the tests. If you have a disability, the Instituto Cervantes offers adapted conditions, so ask when you book. Members of the armed forces have their own route.
nat.disp.5: Age: the order we read names no age. Some advisers say that people over 70 can get a dispensa, and others say that age alone isn't enough, so ask the Ministry.
nat.steps.title: The steps, in order
nat.s1.title: 1. Work out your residence time
nat.s1.text: Find the period that applies to you and the date you reach it. Keep your residence permit valid while you prepare.
nat.s2.title: 2. Sort out any exemption
nat.s2.text: If you may need a dispensa, ask for it now, because it comes before the application and can take six months.
nat.s3.title: 3. Take the exams
nat.s3.text: The rules we read set no order, so you can take the CCSE and the DELE in whichever order suits you. Both are taken in person, and no course is compulsory. The DELE has fixed dates and results take a while, so book early. The order gives a CCSE certificate 4 years from its date, so don't take it too long before you apply.
nat.s3.figures: As far as we could check, the CCSE has {t} questions in {m} minutes and you pass with {pass} correct. Exam centres in Spain list about €85 for the CCSE and about €138 for DELE A2. Check the current figures with the Instituto Cervantes.
nat.s4.title: 4. Collect your documents
nat.s4.text: The regulation names the application form, your birth certificate from your country of origin, your passport, the evidence of integration (the exams), the fee receipt and papers on any special circumstances. Adults also need a criminal record certificate from their country of origin. Foreign documents usually have to be legalised and translated. The Ministry's current list is the one that counts.
nat.s5.title: 5. Pay the fee and apply
nat.s5.text: The fee is paid with form 790, code 026. The 2015 law set it at €100, and most sources give about €104 today, so check the form before you pay. The Ministry of Justice lists an online application and an in-person one.
nat.s6.title: 6. Wait for the decision
nat.s6.text: The regulation gives the Ministry one year from when your application reaches the office. If you have no answer by then, it counts as a refusal. Ask a lawyer what you can do at that point. The Ministry can also say no for reasons of public order or national interest.
nat.s7.title: 7. Take the oath and register
nat.s7.text: If you get a yes, go to the Civil Registry within 180 days of being notified. If you miss this, the grant lapses. There you swear or promise loyalty to the King and obedience to the Constitution and the laws, give up your previous nationality if that applies to you, and ask to be registered. Nationals of Ibero-American countries, Andorra, the Philippines, Equatorial Guinea and Portugal, and people of Sephardic origin, don't have to give it up.
nat.s7.after: Whether your first country still treats you as its citizen depends on its own law, so ask its consulate. Once you are registered, you can apply for a Spanish DNI and passport.
nat.other: This page only covers nationality by residence. Nationality by origin, by option or through family history has its own rules.

dgt.orient.title: The driving licence in Spain: a short orientation
dgt.orient.legal: General orientation, not legal advice. Rules and exam details change. This is how we understood them in November 2026; check the official DGT website (Dirección General de Tráfico, Spain's traffic authority) before you rely on them.
dgt.orient.1: To get a new licence, you pass a theory exam (examen teórico) and a practical exam (examen práctico). Most people go to a driving school (autoescuela), but the DGT says you can also prepare on your own (por libre).
dgt.orient.2: You also need a medical report from an authorised drivers' medical centre (centro de reconocimiento de conductores).
dgt.orient.3: The DGT describes the theory exam as a test of 30 questions with three answer options each, and it has announced a video question about spotting risks. Check the current format and pass mark with the DGT or your driving school.
dgt.orient.4: You may not have to take the theory exam in Spanish. Reports say the category B exam is offered in English, French and German, and in the co-official languages in their regions. Ask which languages you can choose when you apply. Even then, signs, instructions and papers will be in Spanish.
dgt.orient.5: If you already hold a licence from another country, you may be able to use or exchange it (canje) instead of taking the exams. It depends on the country, so check yours with the DGT first.
dgt.orient.practice: For practice questions, use the DGT's own free online tests.
